## Design note

The fastest thing on four wheels in the game and the least suited to a city. Under a tonne, with downforce that would hold it to a ceiling at 250 km/h, it stops and turns at speeds nothing else can follow — on a smooth, wide road. On city streets the 60 mm ride height grounds on every crest, the steering lock makes U-turns a three-point affair and visibility out of the cockpit is poor.

## How this car breaks

Carbon-fibre survival cell that will shrug off a hit at almost any speed — and almost nothing else. The nose is a crushable carbon cone, the floor, wings and bodywork are thin composite that shatters on contact, the engine and gearbox are stressed members behind the tub so rear hits break the car in two, and the suspension wishbones snap rather than bend. Durability class 3 (not 2) with a reinforced nose: at strength 0.9 the 56 km/h frontal crushed 1.91 m (band 0.35-1.3); now ≈ 1.3-1.4 m, a known miss — the generator has no flat prototype profile and the whole 1 m nose cone is sacrificial by design.

## Sources (type)

- series technical regulations for 2010s closed-cockpit spec prototypes (minimum weight, dimensions, restrictor)
- engine-supplier data for restricted 4.2 L prototype V8s
- on-board telemetry figures for the class (braking g, cornering g, top speed)
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, carbon brake hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 384 | 0.70 | 270 |
| pitch | 1850 | 0.72 | 1330 |
| yaw | 2054 | 0.72 | 1480 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.80·W·H = 1.60 m²; Cd = 0.52 → **CdA = 0.830 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = -0.90 / -1.10 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). Add-on aero `aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0.60 F / 0.80 R m² (full-width front splitter and tunnels, venturi floor with a long diffuser, twin-element rear wing at the high-downforce sprint setting). Net downforce Cl·A 1.50 F / 1.90 R m² → 1024 kg at 250 km/h, 44% front (static weight 45% front).

## Engine

4.2 L DOHC 32-valve 90° V8, naturally aspirated through an air restrictor, dry sump, stressed member. Class-typical spec prototype V8 under its restrictor (~420 kW at 9000 rpm, 515 N·m at 6000-6500) per series technical regulations and engine-supplier data. Tiny flywheel, highest revs and strongest engine braking in the roster.

## Drivetrain

6-speed paddle-shift sequential (pneumatic, flat-shift), plated rear LSD, carbon multi-plate clutch. Layout **RWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 100 N·m, power ramp 0.50, coast ramp 0.40. Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 820 N·m. Shift time 0.15 s.

Final drive 3.30, reverse 2.80. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.348 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.35 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 200 kg | 3.00 Hz | 71000 N/m | 2640 N·s/m | 3960 N·s/m | 0.04 m |
| Rear | 247 kg | 3.20 Hz | 99700 N/m | 3470 N·s/m | 5200 N·s/m | 0.06 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **3170 / 6340 N·s/m F, 4160 / 8320 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 0.6°/g with 55% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.198 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 181229 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 93171 F / 124480 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **2500 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 0.5°/g, front share 44%. Bump stops 350000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -3.2° F / -2.2° R, toe -0.10° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 6.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 41 mm + 38 mm + 36 mm → A = 34.7 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.55: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.55·100 bar·34.7 cm²·0.165 m = **6302 N·m**
- Rear: 355 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 36 mm → A = 21.5 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 152 mm, pad μ = 0.52: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.52·100 bar·21.5 cm²·0.152 m = **3413 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 6302 / 3413 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.36), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.28 → **1780 / 960 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 873 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.04×), rear needs 750 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.28×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 1530 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 1780 N·m front / 960 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1710 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 10.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 14.0 m → outer-front path radius 6.85 m, rear-axle-centre radius 5.35 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.511 rad (29.3°)** (outer 26.0°, inner 33.5° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.30). Rack speed 2.4 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/nyx_proto.json`)

289 nodes, 1853 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id nyx_proto --profile coupe --width 1.9 --length 4.65 --height 1.05 --wheelbase 3.0 --mass 195.4 --car-mass 977.1 --clearance 0.06 --front-overhang 1.0 --strength 1.0` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Carbon-fibre survival cell (prototype monocoque, roll hoop and side-intrusion panels): 384 passenger-cell beams (cabin, sills, pillars, roof rails, cross-members) × 1.80 section.
- Aluminium body: 663 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.75…-1.40 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 194 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
- Homologated crash nose (carbon impact structure ahead of the tub): 16 front-rail beams × 1.80 section.
